title: Prevent Locate shortcut from stealing normal search text entry

scope.subject: Keyboard interaction for the restored Search/Places navigator

research_summary: The committed Locate implementation binds the plain letter L inside the search input, which conflicts with ordinary query entry. The existing navigator already uses Enter to activate the current result, so the smallest coherent fix is Shift+Enter for Locate and Enter for Open. This preserves native text entry, requires no new keybinding framework, and leaves the explicit LOCATE button available for pointer users.

sources.finding: Editable combobox patterns reserve printable characters for text editing; action keys should not steal ordinary character input.
KeyboardEvent.shiftKey exposes the Shift modifier without taking over printable text keys.

search_ladder.conclusion: No navigation product change is needed for a local keybinding conflict.
Rendering framework is unrelated to keyboard semantics.
Keep the restored YEIS-style navigator and change only the conflicting activation gesture.
Native KeyboardEvent modifier state fully covers the fix; no shortcut package is needed.

coverage_matrix.capability: allow arbitrary search text including the letter l
coverage_matrix.decision: Printable letters must remain text input.
Shift+Enter reuses the selected-result activation key without adding a second unrelated mnemonic.
Prefer a modifier on the existing Enter action over another letter chord.

candidates.name: Enter opens; Shift+Enter locates
candidates.source: native KeyboardEvent.shiftKey on existing navigator input
candidates.reason: Preserves all printable text, aligns Locate with the existing selected-result activation gesture, and adds no dependency.

candidates.name: Keep plain L as Locate
candidates.reason: Conflicts directly with normal search entry for any query containing l/L.

candidates.name: Use Alt+L for Locate
candidates.reason: Avoids text theft but introduces a new mnemonic chord and can collide with browser/platform menu behaviors; Shift+Enter is more local to result activation.

decision.rationale: Use native Shift+Enter on the existing Enter activation path. Keep Enter=Open, Shift+Enter=Locate, and the visible LOCATE button for pointer users.
decision.fallback: If later accessibility testing prefers a different gesture, keep pointer LOCATE and expose the keyboard mapping through the same activation handler.
